squawks.headline: UK government says ministers are working urgently with India to settle dispute over higher tariffs on Scotch whisky
squawks.detail: The UK government said ministers are working urgently with India on the dispute over Indian demands for higher tariffs on Scotch whisky imports. This follows reports that India is applying an effective 162.5% tariff and tax on bulk Scotch imports.

squawks.headline: BoC Deputy Governor Gravelle says energy price inflation is spreading
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Gravelle said inflation from energy prices is spreading, adding to his earlier remarks on inflation expectations.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barr backs further rate rises if the economy performs as expected, calling inflation too high
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve Governor Barr said inflation is too high and must be brought back to 2% in a timely way, and that the economy is strong with low unemployment. He said he would support further hikes if the economy evolves as expected and will watch the data to decide the Fed's next move.

squawks.headline: US Defense Secretary Hegseth says the oil deal takes the Strait of Hormuz out of the equation
squawks.detail: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the oil deal means the Strait of Hormuz is no longer a factor. No further details of the deal or any market reaction were reported.

squawks.headline: Gold falls 2.9% to $3,737.79/oz, its lowest in more than a year, as hawkish Fed signals lift the dollar
squawks.detail: Gold fell 2.9% to $3,737.79 an ounce, its lowest level in more than a year. The drop was attributed to hawkish Fed signals and expectations of more aggressive rate hikes, which strengthened the dollar.

squawks.headline: US $16bn 20-year Treasury auction prices at 5.459%, level with when-issued; bid-to-cover falls to 2.63
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $16bn of 20-year bonds at a high yield of 5.459%, against 5.469% at the previous sale, with bid-to-cover at 2.63 versus 2.730 last time. Indirect bidders took 60.2%, directs 26.7% and primary dealers 13.1%, and 70.87% of bids at the high yield were allotted.

squawks.headline: French Senate adopts 2027 social security budget that restores pension reform, BFMTV reports
squawks.detail: France's Senate has passed the 2027 social security financing bill in a version that restores the pension reform, according to BFMTV.

squawks.headline: US 20-year Treasury trades at 5.459% when-issued ahead of $16bn auction
squawks.detail: The when-issued 20-year US Treasury yield was 5.459% shortly before the $16 billion auction.

squawks.headline: BoE Governor Bailey signals further rate hikes are likely if the Iran war continues and the labour market firms
squawks.detail: Speaking at the Institute of Economic Development Conference in London, the Governor said a continuing Iran war and a firming labour market were likely to lead to more interest rate rises, City AM reports. He referred to nine months of conflict in the Middle East.

squawks.headline: UK and EU remove 'trusted partnership' wording from latest draft of joint summit statement, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the latest draft of the UK-European Commission joint summit statement no longer refers to a trusted partnership. It says this suggests talks on special status for the UK under the EU's Made in Europe rules are proving difficult.

squawks.headline: Ukrainian attacks have disrupted or shut 15 of Russia's 35 major refineries, industry sources say
squawks.detail: Industry sources say a series of Ukrainian attacks has disrupted or halted operations at 15 of Russia's 35 major oil refineries. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: BoC Deputy Governor Gravelle says anchored inflation expectations make monetary policy more effective
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Gravelle said the Bank's scenarios are meant to keep it accountable and build credibility. He said public trust in returning inflation to around 2% makes businesses less likely to build higher inflation into their prices.

squawks.headline: Fed's Daly says inflation has been too high for too long and backs continuing a measured approach to policy
squawks.detail: San Francisco Fed President Daly said the labour market is stable overall but has little dynamism, and that consumer spending is resilient even among lower-income households, which she called both a strength and a risk. She also said AI could put pressure on other goods and services.

squawks.headline: Yemeni forces carry out drone attacks on Riyadh and southern Saudi Arabia, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say Yemeni forces launched drone attacks on targets in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and in southern parts of the country. This follows Western officials saying Saudi Arabia expects its war with the Houthis to run well into 2027.

squawks.headline: US crude futures extend losses to more than $3/bbl on supply surplus outlook
squawks.detail: US crude futures are reported down by more than $3 a barrel, extending the earlier drop of more than $2. The move is put down to the outlook for surplus supply.

squawks.headline: US crude futures drop more than $2/bbl to their lowest since 28 August on supply surplus outlook
squawks.detail: Front-month US crude futures fell by more than $2 a barrel to the lowest level since 28 August, with the move attributed to expectations of a supply surplus.

squawks.headline: EU Council authorises signing of trade and investment agreements with Indonesia
squawks.detail: The EU Council has given formal authorisation for the EU-Indonesia trade and investment agreements to be signed.

squawks.headline: German coalition agrees one-year cut to electricity taxes for consumers and small businesses
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Germany's ruling coalition agreed on Wednesday to cut electricity taxes for consumers and small businesses for one year, settling a dispute between Chancellor Merz's conservatives and the SPD. Economists have warned about fiscal discipline.

squawks.headline: Brent extends losses after official US inventory data; January contract at $91.95/bbl
squawks.detail: Oil prices kept falling on Wednesday evening after the official US inventory figures were released, according to reports. January Brent crude futures on ICE stood at $91.95 per barrel.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham declines to commit to welfare savings by 2030, a day after saying he would
squawks.detail: City AM reports that at PMQs, when Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch asked whether he would deliver welfare savings in the near term after backing the Alan Milburn review, the Prime Minister said only that he would do everything he could. A day earlier he had said he would make the savings by 2030.

squawks.headline: Trump's envoys tell Russia it is running out of time to reach a Ukraine deal, Kyiv Independent reports
squawks.detail: The Kyiv Independent reports that US President Trump's envoys have warned Moscow that time to secure an agreement on Ukraine is running short. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: BoE Governor Bailey says the Bank is applying system patches at its fastest rate ever to protect its systems
squawks.detail: BoE Governor Andrew Bailey said the Bank is applying patches to protect its systems at the highest rate it has ever done.

squawks.headline: BoE Governor Bailey says the Bank is building a team specialising in the economics of AI
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor said the Bank is setting up a team focused on the economics of artificial intelligence. He did not refer to interest rates in the reported remark.

squawks.headline: Canada's PM Carney says Canada still faces a series of trade issues with the US
squawks.detail: Canadian Prime Minister Carney said a number of trade issues with the US remain unresolved. Earlier, China agreed to cut some tariffs on Canadian imports after talks between Carney and Xi.

squawks.headline: European gas futures drop as much as 5.1% to €81.05/MWh
squawks.detail: European gas futures fell by as much as 5.1% during the session to €81.05 per megawatt-hour.

squawks.headline: BoE Governor Bailey says CPI inflation is likely to peak below 5% because energy prices have eased
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor said UK consumer price inflation is likely to peak below 5%, citing easing energy prices. He made the remarks during comments on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: BoE Governor Bailey says inflation will rise further and calls the rise very frustrating; stronger food inflation has not materialised
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor said, when asked about rising inflation, that it was enormously frustrating and that he expects inflation to go up further. He also said the expected pick-up in food inflation has not happened.

squawks.headline: Czech LNG deal with the US will cover 20% of the country's LNG consumption, industry and trade minister says
squawks.detail: Czech Minister of Industry and Trade Havlicek gave the figure in Warsaw. It refers to the long-term US LNG purchase deal the Czech Republic is finalising.

squawks.headline: Czechia is finalising a 15-20 year deal with the US to buy 1.4 bcm of LNG, industry and trade minister says
squawks.detail: Czech Minister of Industry and Trade Havlicek said in Warsaw that the country is completing a long-term contract with the US, lasting 15 to 20 years, for 1.4 bcm of LNG.

squawks.headline: China and South Korea finish the second phase of free-trade talks; Beijing says it will boost investment between the two countries
squawks.detail: China published a statement on progress towards a trade agreement with South Korea. The statement said the second phase of talks was complete and that both sides would expand investment in each other.

squawks.headline: BoE Governor Bailey says UK growth has improved but more effort is needed, and that the private sector has mainly driven this year's…
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor made the remarks in comments reported on Wednesday afternoon. They follow his earlier remarks the same day on the policy path and labour market slack.

squawks.headline: BoE Governor Bailey says policy is not on a pre-set path and labour market slack has stabilised as growth picks up
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said monetary policy is not on a pre-set path. He added that the margin of slack in the labour market has stabilised as activity growth has picked up.

squawks.headline: US pending home sales fall 4.7% m/m, a bigger drop than the 2% forecast; index slips to 63.0
squawks.detail: US pending home sales fell 4.7% m/m, against a 2% forecast fall and a previous 7.3% decline. The index fell to 63.0 from a revised 66.1.

squawks.headline: Russian oil refining volumes are down 45% since late October after Ukrainian drone strikes, industry sources say
squawks.detail: Industry sources say Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refinery throughput by 45% since late October.

squawks.headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum says Trump told her the US and Mexico are close to a trade deal
squawks.detail: Mexican President Sheinbaum said US President Trump told her the two countries are nearing a trade agreement. This follows her earlier remarks that talks were advancing after their meeting on the sidelines of APEC.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says AI valuations are very ambitious and will eventually be corrected; European economy more resilient than expected
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said AI valuations are very ambitious and stand to be corrected at some point. She added that the European economy has held up much better than anticipated, supported by AI and fiscal policy.

squawks.headline: China agrees to cut some tariffs on Canadian imports after Carney-Xi talks
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that China agreed to reduce some levies on imports from Canada after talks between Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Ottawa is seeking to reduce its trade reliance on the US.

squawks.headline: UK set to conclude food trade deal with EU later this week, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the UK expects to finalise a food trade agreement with Brussels later this week. Under the deal the UK would have to drop its promised ban on foie gras imports.

squawks.headline: Mexico's President Sheinbaum says trade talks with the US are advancing after APEC sideline talks with Trump
squawks.detail: Mexican President Sheinbaum said she discussed trade with President Trump and his team on the sidelines of the APEC meeting. She said the two countries are making progress in their trade talks.

squawks.headline: IEA chief Birol says energy markets have no realistic route back to where they stood before the Iran war
squawks.detail: International Energy Agency executive director Fatih Birol said flows through the Strait of Hormuz could be blocked again, according to City AM.

squawks.headline: US Commerce Department sets new rules to stop some foreign actors using US-based advanced computing power against US security
squawks.detail: A Federal Register notice says the US Commerce Department is setting new rules to stop certain foreign actors from using advanced computing power built on US technology to threaten US national security and foreign policy interests. The notice does not name the countries affected.

squawks.headline: US housing starts rise 9.9% m/m to 1.309M, above forecast; building permits fall 7.4% m/m
squawks.detail: US housing starts came in at 1.309M against a 1.25M forecast and 1.221M previously, a 9.9% monthly rise versus 2.4% expected. Building permits fell 7.4% m/m, against a forecast drop of 1.7% and a previous fall of 0.4%.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia expects its war with the Houthis to run well into 2027, Western officials say
squawks.detail: Two Western officials, citing conversations with Saudi counterparts, say Riyadh expects the conflict to continue well into 2027. They add that Saudi Arabia wants its allies to gain ground in Yemen before any negotiations with the Houthis.

squawks.headline: US Energy Secretary Wright says US LNG will now cover about a third of Poland's yearly gas demand
squawks.detail: US Energy Secretary Wright said in a post on X that there will now be enough American LNG to supply roughly one-third of Poland's annual natural gas demand.

squawks.headline: BoE proposes temporarily easing capital requirements on major banks in downturns to make buffers more usable
squawks.detail: On Wednesday the Bank of England published proposals that would let capital requirements on major banks be eased temporarily during downturns, with the aim of stopping banks from cutting lending too sharply, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises 2bp to 5.12%
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reported that the US 10-year Treasury yield was up 2bp at 5.12% at midday UK time.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says the Fed must reverse its 3 insurance cuts and possibly go further
squawks.detail: Fed Governor Waller said returning rates to their summer 2025 level would not bring inflation down. He also said nothing in AI pricing looks like a bubble, and that his concern over AI financing is limited to banks.

squawks.headline: ECB to discuss raising banks' minimum reserve requirement from 1% to 2% on 25 November, sources say
squawks.detail: Sources familiar with the discussion say the ECB will consider the increase on 25 November, but the decision could be put off until December.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says the Fed should hike 50bp now unless it signals a tougher path in its statement or press conference
squawks.detail: Waller also said the Fed may need to go beyond reversing last year's cuts to bring inflation down and must break the idea that 3% inflation is normal. He added that the December SEP will be of limited use because it is a year-end figure.

squawks.headline: NIESR expects the BoE to hold rates in December and raise them again early next year
squawks.detail: NIESR's monthly CPI tracker says the risk of second-round effects is growing as unemployment falls and inflation expectations rise. It notes that October was the fourth consecutive rise in CPI.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller calls for more aggressive rate hikes, saying inflation is moving the wrong way and broadening
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, Fed Governor Waller said the Fed needs to be somewhat more aggressive with rate hikes to bring inflation down, and noted that about 70% of items in the core services basket are running above 3%, a rise he said is unrelated to oil. He said he is concerned that firms believe they can pass on price rises of 3% or more, and that the Fed may need to shock people out of treating 3% inflation as normal.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says he will keep to Labour's manifesto red lines on the EU
squawks.detail: UK Prime Minister Burnham said the government will respect the red lines on the EU relationship set out in Labour's manifesto. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French foreign minister denies Moscow's claim that France is directly intervening in the war in Ukraine
squawks.detail: The French foreign minister said French military activity in Ukraine is far from the front lines and does not amount to direct participation in the war, according to reports. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says the EU deal will lower food prices
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said the UK's agreement with the EU will lower food prices. The remarks come ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham pledges to cut the welfare bill as fast as possible
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said in parliament that he would do all he could to reduce the welfare bill as quickly as possible. He spoke during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: UK plans to resist EU request to match its tariffs on Chinese goods, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports the position is in a draft communiqué ahead of the UK-EU summit, and that it reduces the chance of Britain gaining access to subsidies and contracts under 'made in Europe' rules.

squawks.headline: ECB's Vujcic says a December rate hike looks very likely as things stand and expects second-round effects in 2027
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Vujcic also said market pricing for 2027 is not unreasonable.

squawks.headline: ECB's Vujcic says fiscal policy must fix fiscal problems and stagflation does not currently look likely
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Vujcic made the remarks on Wednesday. On the same day the ECB's financial stability review called fiscal consolidation overdue.

squawks.headline: Central London house prices fall 7.2% y/y in the year to September, the biggest annual drop since August 2009
squawks.detail: City AM reports that average house prices in central London fell 7.2% in the year to September. The report links the fall to interest rates and higher taxes.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Putin and Trump will mainly discuss Ukraine and current issues at their meeting, and may also cover Iran
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said the two leaders would focus on current issues and Ukraine and might also discuss Iran, Tass reported. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: India reportedly levies effective 162.5% tariff and tax on bulk Scotch imports, above the 150% charged before the UK trade pact
squawks.detail: Sources and a document cited in an exclusive report say India now applies an effective 162.5% combined tariff and tax on bulk Scotch imports. To release blocked shipments, firms must pay 75% of the duty up front and cover the rest with bank guarantees. Pernod and Diageo are reported to be arranging guarantees, while Bacardi has not yet decided.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Putin and Trump will talk at APEC but full negotiations are unlikely
squawks.detail: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said Putin and Trump are unlikely to have time for full negotiations at the APEC summit, but the two leaders will speak.

squawks.headline: German 7-year Bund auction sells at 3.27% average yield, down from 3.36%; bid-to-cover rises to 1.5
squawks.detail: Germany's 7-year Bund auction gave an average yield of 3.27%, compared with 3.36% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.5, up from 1.4 last time.

squawks.headline: EU's Dombrovskis says Ukraine loan could also be repaid from profits on immobilised Russian assets
squawks.detail: European Commission Vice-President Dombrovskis said the proposed Ukraine loan could also be repaid from profits on immobilised Russian assets and would help build joint European capabilities with Ukraine. Commission President von der Leyen said all 27 member states want to support Ukraine and that she is confident the measure will be agreed by 2027.

squawks.headline: Xi calls for stable and constructive China-US relations as he greets Trump in Shenzhen
squawks.detail: Xinhua says China's President Xi made the remarks when he met US President Trump at Shenzhen airport. Earlier, China warned the US it would retaliate over new curbs on AI chips.

squawks.headline: EU's von der Leyen says Commission will present a 22nd Russia sanctions package next week
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen also said external partners should cover another third of Ukraine's 2027 financing needs, alongside the proposed €45bn EU instrument for 2027. She said the loan would help integrate the European and Ukrainian defence industries.

squawks.headline: European Commission proposes €45bn loan to Ukraine for 2027 financing needs, repayable from Russian war reparations
squawks.detail: Commission President von der Leyen said the loan comprises €20bn for budget support and €25bn for military needs, and that Ukraine would only repay once Russia has covered the damage. She said the EU would give Ukraine maximum support and put maximum pressure on Russia.

squawks.headline: Eurozone final October CPI confirmed at 4.0% y/y; core revised up to 2.6%, above 2.5% forecast
squawks.detail: The final eurozone October reading puts headline inflation at 4.0% y/y, matching the estimate, and 0.5% m/m against a 0.4% forecast. Core inflation is 2.6% y/y, compared with a 2.5% forecast and 2.5% previously.

squawks.headline: Most Gulf stock markets fall as US-Iran hostilities escalate
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that most Gulf bourses fell in early trade on Wednesday. Gulf states had intercepted Iranian and Houthi missiles and drones after a US strike on Qeshm Island.

squawks.headline: Cornwall Insight forecasts the UK energy price cap will rise 26% in January to £2,166 a year
squawks.detail: The energy consultancy estimates that the January cap will add £443 to annualised household bills, taking them to £2,166, according to City AM.

squawks.headline: German cabinet approves nominating Brunnermeier as ECB chief economist
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the German cabinet has approved putting Markus Brunnermeier forward as the European Central Bank's chief economist.

squawks.headline: ECB compares the AI borrowing surge to the run-up to the subprime bubble
squawks.detail: The ECB says the current wave of AI-related borrowing has historic parallels with the subprime bubble, the FT reports. It raises concerns that hyperscalers are building up trillions of dollars of off-balance-sheet commitments through contracts with other technology groups.

squawks.headline: ONS: UK house prices rise 1.2% y/y to £273,000 in September; private rents up 3.8% y/y to £1,411 in October
squawks.detail: The ONS reports that average UK house prices rose 1.2% to £273,000 in the 12 months to September 2026. It also reports that average monthly private rents rose 3.8% to £1,411 in the 12 months to October 2026.

squawks.headline: ECB's Vujcic says hedge fund activity partly drove this year's rapid spread widening, though the effect was short-lived
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Vujcic said hedge fund positions and their unwinding can move markets very rapidly, and that a sharp market correction could cut consumption in Europe and the US through the wealth effect. He also said the ECB had discussed opening its balance sheet to funds and decided against it, though the idea may return.

squawks.headline: FT reports the British energy price cap is set to rise above £2,000 in January
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the British household energy price cap is due to rise above £2,000 from January. It adds that reduced government support means households will pay more for energy in real terms than during the inflation shock after the invasion of Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Russia's Novatek to redirect LNG supply away from the EU market, with most going to China
squawks.detail: Interfax reports that Russian LNG producer Novatek will redirect LNG supply away from the EU market and that most of it will go to China. Novatek has also signed a contract to supply LNG to Turkey, Interfax reports.

squawks.headline: Iceland's central bank says inflation is still too high and expectations remain above target
squawks.detail: Iceland's central bank said inflation remains too high, inflation expectations are above target and the outlook is highly uncertain.

squawks.headline: ECB says fiscal consolidation is overdue and sovereign risk could be repriced further
squawks.detail: The ECB said strict application of EU fiscal rules is essential and that fiscal consolidation is overdue, warning that sovereign risk could be repriced further. It added that wider French spreads point to risks specific to that country.

squawks.headline: ECB stability review says market discipline should push indebted states to fiscal correction and flags French spreads
squawks.detail: The ECB's Financial Stability Review says market discipline should push highly indebted countries to correct their fiscal policy. It also says the widening in French spreads points to risks specific to France.

squawks.headline: BoE begins issuing regular statements in response to UK inflation data, except in the run-up to MPC meetings
squawks.detail: An economics journalist notes the Bank of England has started publishing regular statements after UK inflation releases. They will not be issued in the period before MPC meetings.

squawks.headline: Finland's President Stubb says Ukraine peace talks are moving in the right direction
squawks.detail: Stubb described himself as cautiously optimistic about the talks on Ukraine. He also said Europe had organised itself for the peace negotiations.

squawks.headline: BoE says it will keep setting rates to bring inflation back to the 2% target and keep it there
squawks.detail: The Bank of England said this in its response to Wednesday's UK inflation data for October.

squawks.headline: BoE says it expects inflation to rise further by mid-2026 next year as pipeline cost pressures feed through
squawks.detail: The Bank of England issued a statement responding to Wednesday's UK inflation data. It said it expects inflation to rise further by the middle of next year because of cost pressures already in the pipeline.

squawks.headline: Xi tells Putin China and Russia should deepen cooperation
squawks.detail: Chinese President Xi Jinping told Russian President Vladimir Putin that the two countries should deepen their cooperation, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

squawks.headline: French finance minister Lescure says 2027 budget needs a bigger effort than planned and 1% growth forecast may be cut
squawks.detail: France's finance minister Lescure said the 2027 budget will require a larger effort than previously planned. He also said the 1% growth forecast for 2027 risks being revised down.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US has struck a new trade deal with the Philippines, citing gains for farmers and energy
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he had made a new and different trade deal with the Philippines after meetings there on trade and national security, and said it would benefit US farmers and the energy sector. No terms were given.

squawks.headline: Futures cut odds of a December BoE rate hike to 80% from 90% after UK CPI data
squawks.detail: UK interest rate futures put the chance of a Bank of England rate rise in December at 80%, down from 90%, after the release of October's UK CPI figures.

squawks.headline: Traders scale back BoE rate hike bets and now price 91bp of tightening by end-2027
squawks.detail: Money markets have reduced expectations for Bank of England rate rises and now price 91bp of tightening by the end of 2027, according to a market report.

squawks.headline: UK RPI rises to 4.2% y/y in October, above 4.1% forecast; up 0.6% m/m
squawks.detail: Retail price inflation rose to 4.2% y/y from 3.9% previously, against a 4.1% forecast, and was up 0.6% m/m against a 0.5% estimate. RPI excluding mortgage interest payments rose to 4.1% y/y from 3.9%, and the index stood at 424.5.

squawks.headline: UK CPI rises to 3.6% y/y in October as forecast; services inflation holds at 3.7%, below 3.8% forecast
squawks.detail: October figures show headline CPI at 3.6% y/y against 3.5% previously, services CPI at 3.7% against a 3.8% forecast, CPIH at 3.7% against 3.6% previously, and core CPI up 0.3% m/m against 0.2% previously. The Guardian reports that higher energy prices were behind the rise, with the Iran war pushing up the cost of oil.

squawks.headline: UK core CPI holds at 2.8% y/y as forecast; headline CPI rises 0.5% m/m, matching expectations
squawks.detail: UK core CPI was 2.8% year on year, unchanged from the previous month and in line with forecasts. Headline CPI rose 0.5% month on month against 0.4% previously, and RPI rose 0.6% m/m against a 0.5% forecast and 0.1% previously.

squawks.headline: UK PPI input prices jump 10.8% y/y, well above 9.2% forecast; output prices rise 5.1% y/y as expected
squawks.detail: UK input producer prices rose 2.2% m/m against a 0.8% forecast and 10.8% y/y, up from 8.3%. Output prices rose 0.4% m/m, below the 0.6% forecast, and 5.1% y/y, in line with forecasts and up from 4.6%.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham pledges sweeping welfare overhaul for young people and hints at changes for older claimants
squawks.detail: The prime minister committed to reforms following the Milburn review, whose author argued for extending them to over-24s, the FT reports. Labour MPs who led last year's rebellion against £5bn of benefit cuts have backed the proposals.

squawks.headline: Germany to cut its electricity tax to the EU minimum for 2027 as a temporary step, with a permanent cut intended
squawks.detail: The German government says the electricity tax will fall to the European minimum level for 2027 on a temporary basis and that it intends to make the reduction permanent.

squawks.headline: Japan's 20-year government bond yield edges up to 3.780% after auction
squawks.detail: The 20-year JGB yield rose slightly to 3.780% after the auction result was released on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: Iran's army says it targeted US drone and missile sites at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem base
squawks.detail: Iranian state media carried the army's claim. The WSJ separately reports that Iran has attacked Kuwait and Bahrain as the conflict over the Strait of Hormuz intensifies.

squawks.headline: Xi calls for free and open trade without investment barriers as he opens APEC summit in Shenzhen
squawks.detail: In his opening speech at the APEC summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping called for free and open trade without barriers to investment, Reuters reported. He is due to meet his US and Russian counterparts at the summit.

squawks.headline: Putin tells APEC CEO summit that restrictions on Russia raise costs and Europe is bearing the impact
squawks.detail: Speaking at the APEC CEO summit in China, Russian President Putin said sanctions on Moscow create artificial barriers that raise costs and hurt Europe, and that the US dollar's share of Russia's trade has fallen sharply. He also said Russia is ready to widen export markets for food and fertiliser, and that a Trump–Xi meeting could bring significant gains.

squawks.headline: China warns the US it will retaliate over new curbs on AI chips
squawks.detail: CNBC reports that Beijing has warned Washington of retaliation over new US rules restricting China's access to advanced US-made AI chips. Semafor reports that Singapore is pressing US officials for details of the rules.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda warns long-term rates could rise if bond buying is seen as backing government fiscal measures
squawks.detail: BoJ Governor Ueda said the bank will take account of the effect of a food tax cut on underlying inflation when setting policy, and that yen weakness is an upside risk to food prices through higher import costs. He said long-term borrowing costs are set by the market and the bank is ready to adjust its market operations if long-term yields surge excessively.

squawks.headline: PBOC sets the yuan midpoint at its strongest level since July 2022
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China's latest daily fixing put the yuan midpoint at its strongest level since July 2022.

squawks.headline: US Secretary of State Rubio rules out an imminent Iranian threat to the US homeland
squawks.detail: Rubio made the remarks as the US and Iran exchanged fire in the Gulf. He also said authorities had found no evidence linking recent tech outages to malicious actors.

squawks.headline: BoJ's Ueda signals more rate rises and says the bank can act flexibly if long-term yields spike disproportionately
squawks.detail: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said further policy rate increases would be guided by the economy, prices and financial markets, that monetary conditions remain easy and that inflation needs to settle around 2%. He also said long-term rates could rise if the bank appears to support fiscal policy through bond buying, and that a soft yen may push up food prices.

squawks.headline: Bahrain's military says its air defences repelled a series of Iranian attacks on Wednesday
squawks.detail: Bahrain's Defence Force described the attacks as part of a continued hostile approach by Iran. The Interior Ministry later gave the all-clear, nearly an hour after it had warned of a possible threat amid exchanges of fire between the US and Iran.

squawks.headline: EU lawmakers agree measures to speed up approvals for renewables, power grids and energy storage
squawks.detail: European lawmakers agreed to shorten approval timelines for renewable energy projects, electricity grids and energy storage facilities.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says the Fed will likely need to raise rates again but rejects a shift to a more aggressive path
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that New York Fed President John Williams said on Tuesday that further rate rises will likely be needed to counter high inflation. He argued against moving to a more aggressive pace of tightening.

squawks.headline: Iranian media report air raid sirens at US bases in Kuwait and several explosions heard in the country
squawks.detail: Fars News reported air raid sirens at US bases in Kuwait, and IRIB News, citing Arabic media, reported several explosions. The reports follow the US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island earlier today and have not been confirmed.

squawks.headline: Qatar PM says Doha is still working to broker an agreement between Iran and the US
squawks.detail: Qatar's prime minister said the country's diplomatic efforts to secure a deal between Iran and the US are continuing, Iranian state news agency IRNA reports. The statement follows reported US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island earlier in the day.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack backs small, steady rate hikes but says larger increases may be needed if inflation expectations become entrenched
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack pointed to broad inflation pressures from tariffs, energy costs and AI-related investment. She said further hikes may be needed to cool demand without significantly weakening the labour market.

squawks.headline: Milburn youth unemployment review proposes tax cuts for businesses that hire young people
squawks.detail: The Guardian reports that Alan Milburn's review of youth unemployment recommends tax cuts for employers taking on young people. It says the review may clash with unions and the Labour left over workers' rights and the minimum wage.

squawks.headline: Britain joins Germany in rejecting Pentagon criticism of Ukraine's deep strikes on Russian oil infrastructure
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Germany and Britain on Tuesday rejected Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby's view that Ukraine's deep strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and commercial warehouses were ineffective and risked hardening Russian resolve. Reuters reports the German minister called the criticism stupid.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says AI financing is becoming more opaque and complex but sees no financial stability risk from AI yet
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said financing linked to AI is growing more opaque and complex, though he does not yet see it as a risk to financial stability. He again named cyber security as an ongoing concern.

squawks.headline: UK outlines its planned package of EU agreements ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that on Tuesday the UK government set out the broad shape of the agreements it hopes to reach at this week's summit. The package includes a youth experience programme, a food trade deal and closer cooperation on carbon emissions.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says the Fed will return inflation to 2% in a timely manner and flags cyber security as a continuing concern
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams made the comments in further remarks on Tuesday evening, saying the Fed will bring inflation back to its 2% target in a timely way. He also named cyber security as an ongoing area of worry.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says demand is clearly outpacing supply and financial markets are working very well
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams also said he does not yet see a financial stability risk from AI. The remarks came in further comments on 17 November.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says tariffs are mostly behind us and financial conditions still broadly support growth
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said the tariff effect is largely over and financial conditions have normalised somewhat but remain supportive of growth. He also pointed to increasingly opaque and complex financing of AI.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says inflation is stubbornly high but the situation does not call for dramatic policy action
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said shocks from tariffs and energy are still feeding into inflation readings, with signs of spillover into broader inflation data. He described the economy as resilient and the labour market as solid.

squawks.headline: US official says fighter jets hit an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defence
squawks.detail: A US military official said US fighter aircraft struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island. A US official told Axios the strike was self-defence after Iran targeted US personnel and assets.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says the US economy is strong and getting stronger, and inflation is not moving in the right direction
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said the Fed still has more work to do to bring inflation back to 2%.

squawks.headline: Iran says it is seriously pursuing a diplomatic way out of the impasse, ISNA reports
squawks.detail: Iran's ISNA news agency reports that Tehran is seriously pursuing a diplomatic end to the impasse. The report follows US strikes on Qeshm Island and tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz earlier today.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine's security service carried out the attack on the Crimea bridge
squawks.detail: Ukrainian President Zelenskiy said the Security Service of Ukraine and other services carried out the attack, which he said hit a key Russian military supply route in the south with missiles and drones. He said Ukraine had long warned Russia over its attacks on bridges, cities and energy infrastructure.

squawks.headline: German Defence Minister Pistorius rejects criticism of Ukraine's deep strikes on Russian military targets
squawks.detail: Germany's defence minister said strikes on non-civilian targets in Russia should be seen as legal and legitimate, and called criticism of them foolish. He said Russia's daily attacks on Ukraine's energy, water and heating infrastructure should be condemned instead.

squawks.headline: NATO's Rutte backs Ukraine's deep strikes, saying Russia's war machine must be disabled
squawks.detail: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte backed Ukraine's deep strikes on Russia, saying it is important to disable Russia's war machine. His remarks came after a senior US official criticised the strikes for risking escalation.

squawks.headline: Houthis say they attacked two sections of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline with drones
squawks.detail: In two statements, Yemen's Houthis said they used two drones against the pipeline in the Riyadh area and then three more against another section. No damage, disruption to supply or market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: US Democratic senator files bill to revoke China's normal trade status before Trump-Xi meeting
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that US Senator Tammy Baldwin introduced legislation on Tuesday to remove China's normal trade status and favourable tariff treatment. The bill comes days before President Trump and President Xi meet for the third time this year to discuss their trade truce.

squawks.headline: Fed Governor Cook refuses to attend the hearing convened by Trump, citing the Fed's independence
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Fed Governor Lisa Cook will not attend the hearing called by President Trump. She said taking part in proceedings she considers unfair would put at risk the central bank's unique status and independence.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister says regional security should be built by regional states without foreign interference
squawks.detail: Iranian reports cite Foreign Minister Araghchi as saying all countries in the region believe security should come from within the region, without outside interference. The remarks follow reported US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says some of Milburn's reforms will be dealt with in the Budget
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said some of Alan Milburn's welfare and youth employment reforms are for the Budget, Sky News reported.

squawks.headline: Welsh government's first multiyear Budget puts over £1.5bn of capital spending into social homes over three years
squawks.detail: Inside Housing reports that the Plaid Cymru-led Welsh government's first full Budget sets aside more than £1.5bn over three years towards its target of 20,000 homes.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says an EU deal could lower power and grocery costs
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said a deal with the EU could reduce the cost of electricity and groceries. He made the remark as he set out the government's position on the UK's future relationship with the EU.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says there is no rush to settle long-term EU relationship and next steps will come later this year
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said there was no hurry to decide the UK's long-term relationship with the EU. He said the government would set out its next steps on that relationship later this year.

squawks.headline: Senior US official criticises Ukraine's deep strikes on Russia, citing risk of escalation
squawks.detail: A senior US official criticised Ukraine's long-range strikes inside Russia and pointed to the risk of escalation, according to a market news report. The report did not name the official and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister calls for continued regional consultations after talks with Qatari delegation in Muscat
squawks.detail: Iranian state news agency reports Foreign Minister Araghchi met a Qatari delegation in Oman's capital and stressed the need for ongoing consultations among countries in the region. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister rejects media reports of an Iranian plot to use chemical weapons in Washington
squawks.detail: Iran's foreign minister dismissed reports from the past 72 hours that Iran planned a chemical weapons attack in Washington and was building missile bases under dams. He compared them to propaganda before the Iraq war and said Israel was behind them.

squawks.headline: An official confirms the US has attacked Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: An official confirmed the US attack on Qeshm Island. Earlier reports of the strike were unconfirmed or came from Iranian media.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says inflation is moving the wrong way and housing is the only sector where she sees rates restricting activity
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said yields are being pushed up by expectations for growth and for the Fed, and that inflation is heading in the wrong direction. She also said housing is the one part of the economy where she sees rates holding activity back.

squawks.headline: Atlanta Fed interim President Venable says inflation is still too high and the job market is stable
squawks.detail: Venable, interim president of the Atlanta Fed, commented on inflation and the labour market on 17 November. Posts in the batch report no figures and no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says intervening in markets is harder during a tightening cycle
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said market intervention is more difficult while policy is being tightened. She made the remarks during her earlier comments on Fed and Treasury coordination in market stress.

squawks.headline: Iran's IRGC navy says a fourth tanker has caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Fars News, citing the IRGC navy, reported that a fourth tanker caught fire in the east of the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours. Iran had earlier reported that a third tanker hit a sea mine there.

squawks.headline: US NAHB housing market index falls to 25 in November against 29 forecast; business inventories rise 0.5% m/m
squawks.detail: The NAHB homebuilder sentiment index fell to 25 in November, from 29 the previous month and below the 29 forecast. US business inventories rose 0.5% m/m, in line with forecast, after 0.4% previously.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says Fed and Treasury can coordinate on market stress and Fed is better placed to act in extreme dislocation
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said the Fed and Treasury can work together during market stress while the Fed keeps its independence on monetary policy. She also said the Fed is now better positioned to act when markets are severely dislocated.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says her views on monetary tightening are unchanged since yesterday
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said her views on tightening monetary policy have not changed since yesterday. She also said the US Treasury and the Fed have different objectives in the bond market.

squawks.headline: France rejects Russia's claim that French troops are taking part in the Ukraine war, calling it absurd
squawks.detail: France dismissed the Russian claim that French forces are involved in the war in Ukraine. Earlier, Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov said Moscow would treat French troops deployed in Ukraine as direct participation in the war.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says the Fed should agree principles for Treasury market interventions in advance, while markets are calm
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack told a Brookings Institution event that any interventions should be temporary and targeted, with an exit strategy and timely sale of holdings once stability returns, and that she supports enhancements to the standing repo facility. Her prepared remarks did not address the economic or monetary policy outlook.

squawks.headline: Hungary's central bank leaves interest rates unchanged after a split vote, Governor Varga says
squawks.detail: Hungarian central bank governor Varga said policymakers decided to keep rates on hold and that the vote was divided. The post gave no rate level or vote breakdown.

squawks.headline: US October capacity utilisation slips to 76.4%, below 76.8% forecast; manufacturing output rises 0.3% m/m
squawks.detail: Figures from the US October industrial production report show capacity utilisation at 76.4%, down from 76.9% previously. Manufacturing output rose 0.3% m/m against a 0.2% forecast, and industrial production growth eased to 2.1% y/y from 2.25%.

squawks.headline: US industrial production falls 0.4% m/m in October, against 0.1% rise forecast; previous month 0.7%
squawks.detail: US industrial production fell 0.4% month on month, compared with a forecast of a 0.1% rise and 0.7% growth in the previous month.

squawks.headline: Fed's Waller says the Fed will back responsible payments innovation and makes no comment on monetary policy
squawks.detail: Fed Governor Waller said the Fed will support innovation in payment systems, which he described as still at an early stage, and said traditional money and payment systems still play a key role. He did not comment on monetary policy or the economic outlook.

squawks.headline: Lawyer for Fed Governor Cook threatens to stay away from White House mortgage fraud hearing next month
squawks.detail: In a letter seen by Reuters on Tuesday, a lawyer for Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook called the planned White House hearing into mortgage fraud allegations unfair. The letter says Cook has no legal obligation to take part.

squawks.headline: Iran's Sepah News reports US air strikes on Qeshm Island, following earlier unconfirmed reports
squawks.detail: Iran's Sepah News reports US air strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island. Earlier reports of the strike had been unconfirmed. The posts report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iran's navy says a third tanker has hit a sea mine and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iranian state news agency IRNA, citing Iran's navy, reported a third tanker struck a naval mine and caught fire east of Hormuz. Earlier, Iranian state media reported that a liquefied gas carrier and an oil tanker had hit mines in the strait.

squawks.headline: US Treasury yields climb after US data; 10-year up 1.82bp at 5.139%, 2-year up 2.39bp at 4.851%
squawks.detail: US Treasury yields rose after the release of US economic data. The 10-year note was last up 1.82bp at 5.139% and the 2-year was up 2.39bp at 4.851%.

squawks.headline: Unconfirmed reports say the US has struck Iran's Qeshm Island after an Iranian attack in Bahrain earlier today
squawks.detail: Israel's N12 News cites unofficial sources linked to Iran as reporting US attacks on Qeshm Island. The reports describe the strikes as a response to an Iranian attack in Bahrain on Tuesday morning; there is no official confirmation.

squawks.headline: US retail sales rise 6.8% y/y in October, up from 6.29% in the previous month
squawks.detail: The annual figure was released with the October US retail sales report, which showed a 0.2% monthly rise. The previous month's annual rate was 6.29%.

squawks.headline: US import prices rise 1.1% m/m, above 0.7% forecast; export prices up 1.1% against 0.5% expected
squawks.detail: US import prices rose 1.1% m/m, matching the previous reading and above the 0.7% forecast. Export prices rose 1.1% m/m, against a 0.5% forecast and 2.2% previously.

squawks.headline: Canada's Carney and Mexico's Sheinbaum restate their commitment to renewing the USMCA trade agreement
squawks.detail: A joint statement says the Canadian Prime Minister and the Mexican President reaffirmed their commitment to renewing the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement.

squawks.headline: US retail sales rise 0.2% m/m in October, above 0.1% forecast; core sales up 0.6% against 0.4% expected
squawks.detail: US headline retail sales grew 0.2% m/m, compared with a 0.1% forecast and 0.8% previously. Core retail sales rose 0.6% m/m, against a 0.4% forecast and 0.9% previously.

squawks.headline: Dollar returns to levels last seen in April 2025 on rising rate expectations; euro falls to 19-month low of $1.0982
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the US dollar has recovered all of its 'liberation day' losses as US rate expectations rise. LSEG data show the euro at a 19-month low of $1.0982.

squawks.headline: US ADP weekly employment change rises to 23.75K from 19.75K
squawks.detail: ADP's weekly private payrolls estimate came in at 23.75K, against 19.75K the previous week. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Destatis revises German October HICP up to 2.9% y/y from 2.8%
squawks.detail: The German statistics office also revised October CPI to -0.1% m/m from -0.2%.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says monetary policy needs to respond immediately and AI is bringing forward demand and investment
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem made the further remarks after earlier saying several rate hikes are likely needed before spring.

squawks.headline: Quad statement voices grave concern over economic coercion and arbitrary export restrictions, and pledges to secure supply chains
squawks.detail: A Quad joint statement opposes unilateral or coercive moves to change the status quo and commits to secure critical supply chains and protect freedom of navigation. It also announces closer cooperation on cybersecurity and affirms the AI accelerator.

squawks.headline: McFadden says the government will publish a white paper on its jobs settlement plans in the new year
squawks.detail: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said a white paper setting out the jobs settlement plans will be published in the new year. The announcement follows the Milburn welfare review, which put potential savings at £3.8bn a year by 2036.

squawks.headline: Work and Pensions Secretary McFadden says the PM and cabinet back the need for an entirely new system for young people
squawks.detail: UK Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said the Prime Minister and cabinet have endorsed the need for a whole new system for young people. The remarks come as the Milburn welfare review is published.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says several rate hikes are likely needed before spring and warns high inflation may persist
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said acting soon is the best way to ease price pressures without hurting jobs and growth, and that inflation is most likely to stay elevated unless the Fed raises rates. He also said bond yields would rise if the public doubted the Fed's resolve, and that he was optimistic above-trend GDP growth would continue.

squawks.headline: China's commerce ministry opposes US chip export curb and says it will take countermeasures if the US goes ahead
squawks.detail: China's commerce ministry said it strongly opposes the US move to curb chip exports and will respond with countermeasures if Washington insists on it.

squawks.headline: Trump signs trade deal with Thailand; Thailand to remove all tariffs on US exports
squawks.detail: Trump signed the deal with Thailand's Prime Minister on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. He said Thailand will remove all tariffs on US exports and substantial non-tariff barriers, including on US vehicles, with details to be finalised in the coming weeks.

squawks.headline: Houthis threaten Saudi interests and facilities in retaliation for Saudi strikes on Sana'a province
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthis said Saudi attacks on Sana'a province and other provinces would be answered, and named Saudi interests and facilities as targets. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Hungary says it has an extension letting it import Russian oil without the risk of US sanctions
squawks.detail: Hungary's foreign ministry said on 17 November that it has received an extension that lets it keep importing Russian oil without exposure to US sanctions. The ministry did not give the length of the extension.

squawks.headline: Russian Deputy PM Novak orders oil refineries restored more quickly, reports say
squawks.detail: Reports say Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has ordered work to restore the country's oil refineries to be speeded up. No timetable or volumes were given.

squawks.headline: Milburn says his youth employment plan will save only £200m a year, and not until 2036
squawks.detail: The Guardian reports that Alan Milburn, author of the welfare review, says most of the money saved from benefit cuts for young people will go towards funding a new job support system.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is treating a possible Iranian threat to Washington very seriously
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the US is taking a possible Iranian threat to Washington very seriously. He had earlier warned Iran of an unprecedented response to any such threat. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Polish Prime Minister Tusk says Poland will freeze household gas prices
squawks.detail: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the government will freeze gas prices for households. The report gave no further details on the level or duration of the freeze.

squawks.headline: Iran's foreign minister briefs the Sultan of Oman on an initiative to end the war
squawks.detail: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi held talks on the region with the Sultan of Oman and briefed him on an initiative to end the war. He said Iran has always been serious about diplomacy.

squawks.headline: US administration presses ahead with plan to block imports of Chinese data centre equipment despite tech industry lobbying
squawks.detail: Reuters reports, citing people briefed on the matter, that the Trump administration is moving forward with the curb despite pushback from Amazon, Google, Meta and other US technology companies.

squawks.headline: Milburn says his welfare plan could cut the benefits bill before the next election, with full savings taking years
squawks.detail: Alan Milburn called for an overhaul of the welfare state ahead of publishing his youth unemployment report, the Guardian reports. He said the bill could fall before the next election but the overall savings would take years to arrive.

squawks.headline: BofA fund manager survey shows investors at their smallest bond underweight since November 2025
squawks.detail: The Bank of America fund manager survey shows investors at their smallest underweight in bonds since November 2025. A net 32% of respondents expect global CPI to be lower in 12 months.

squawks.headline: Trump says he will push Xi and Putin to help end the war in Ukraine
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he would press China's President Xi and Russia's President Putin to help bring the Ukraine war to an end. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says a Russia-Ukraine deal is very close and he would meet Putin separately if possible
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks on the sidelines of Quad talks with the leaders of Japan, India and Australia. He said he would hold a separate meeting with Putin if one could be arranged.

squawks.headline: Trump warns Iran of an unprecedented response to any threat on Washington; Tehran rejects CNN dirty bomb report
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the US takes the threat very seriously and that this is why Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson called a CNN report of a possible Iranian plan to set off a dirty bomb in Washington baseless.

squawks.headline: European Commission raises euro zone growth forecasts on AI-driven exports and halves its GDP projections for France
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Commission's latest forecasts raise the euro zone growth outlook as the AI boom lifts exports. The forecasts also show the bloc's largest economies diverging, with France's GDP projections halved.

squawks.headline: EU's Dombrovskis says second-round inflation effects are appearing in the economy
squawks.detail: European Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said second-round inflation effects are now being seen in the economy.

squawks.headline: Russia's Lavrov says Moscow would treat French troops deployed in Ukraine as direct participation in the war
squawks.detail: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Moscow would regard any deployment of French soldiers in Ukraine as direct participation in the conflict.

squawks.headline: German 2-year Schatz auction clears at 3.1% with bid-to-cover of 1.8
squawks.detail: The German 2-year Schatz auction produced an average yield of 3.1%, up from 3.08% at the previous sale. The bid-to-cover ratio was 1.8, up from 1.3 last time.

squawks.headline: FT says Berlin's choice of Brunnermeier for the ECB board seals a deal with France for Spain's de Cos to lead the ECB
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Germany's pick of Markus Brunnermeier as its ECB board nominee consolidates an agreement with France under which Pablo Hernández de Cos would become ECB president.

squawks.headline: Qatar says its mediation between the US and Iran is continuing
squawks.detail: Qatar said its efforts to mediate between the US and Iran are still under way. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: European Commission puts euro zone inflation at 3.2% in 2026, easing to 3.1% in 2027; GDP growth 1.2% in both years
squawks.detail: The European Commission's forecasts put euro zone inflation at 2.1% in 2028 and GDP growth at 1.3% that year. They show the aggregate budget deficit rising to 3.5% of GDP in 2026 from 3.0%, then to 3.8% by 2028, and public debt rising to 89.6% of GDP in 2026 and 91.3% by 2028.

squawks.headline: German ZEW economic sentiment rises to 35.6, beating 28.8 forecast; current conditions improve to -33.2
squawks.detail: The German ZEW economic sentiment index came in at 35.6, against a 28.8 forecast and 28.1 previously, while the current conditions index was -33.2, against a -35.3 forecast and -35.9 previously. The eurozone ZEW expectations index rose to 26.5 from 18.5.

squawks.headline: Germany to back Spain's de Cos for ECB president, sources say
squawks.detail: Two sources say Germany will support the Spanish candidate, Pablo Hernández de Cos, for the ECB presidency. This follows the German government's nomination of Markus Brunnermeier for the post of ECB chief economist.

squawks.headline: Iranian state media say a liquefied gas carrier and an oil tanker are on fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines
squawks.detail: Iranian state media, citing the Revolutionary Guards, report that both vessels caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz. No market reaction is reported in the post.

squawks.headline: Iraq's oil minister puts initial Kirkuk-Ceyhan export capacity at 120,000 bpd, rising gradually to 500,000 bpd
squawks.detail: Iraq's oil minister says crude exports via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline will start at 120,000 barrels per day. He says capacity will be increased step by step until it reaches 500,000 barrels per day.

squawks.headline: Iraq's oil minister says crude exports through the Iraq-Turkey pipeline have resumed
squawks.detail: Iraq's oil minister said crude pumping for export has restarted via the Iraq-Turkey pipeline. No volumes were given.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy confirms Ukraine's military struck Russia's Crimean bridge, calling it a response to strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said the strike was the seventh stage of an operation run over several weeks by the SBU and the General Staff. He described it as retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure.

squawks.headline: German Chancellor backs proposing Brunnermeier for ECB chief economist post, government sources say
squawks.detail: Government sources say the German Chancellor supports the decision to put forward Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB role. The finance minister has already nominated him, and the cabinet is due to decide tomorrow.

squawks.headline: Italy's final CPI is revised up to 5.5% y/y from 5.4%; final HICP confirmed at 5.6%
squawks.detail: Italy's final October CPI rose 1% m/m against a 0.9% forecast, and annual CPI came in at 5.5% against a forecast of 5.4%. Final HICP matched expectations at 1.2% m/m and 5.6% y/y.

squawks.headline: Russia says no date is set for the next round of Ukraine talks and calls Ukraine joining NATO unacceptable
squawks.detail: Russian officials said no date has been fixed for the next round of Ukraine peace talks, according to Tass and other reports. Russia's foreign ministry, via Sergei Ryabkov, said Ukraine's entry into NATO is unacceptable to Moscow, Interfax reported.

squawks.headline: Russia says it has had no response yet to its security proposals
squawks.detail: Russia said it has not yet received any feedback on its security proposals, Interfax reported, as Ukraine peace talks continue.

squawks.headline: Russia says there is no understanding yet on continuing Ukraine peace talks
squawks.detail: Russia said there was no understanding yet on continuing the Ukraine talks, Interfax reported. The Kremlin had earlier said the next round of Russia-Ukraine-US talks had been agreed.

squawks.headline: Germany's finance minister nominates Markus Brunnermeier for ECB chief economist; cabinet to decide tomorrow
squawks.detail: The German Finance Ministry says the finance minister has put forward Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB chief economist post. It says the German cabinet is due to decide on the nomination tomorrow.

squawks.headline: UK Milburn welfare review puts potential savings at £3.8bn a year by 2036
squawks.detail: The Milburn welfare review estimates that its proposals could save £3.8bn a year by 2036. The review is due to propose cutting sickness benefits for under-25s and spending more on employment support.
